entry.title: Re: UI5 manifest.json not accessible in SAP Build PA
entry.content:
The app is deployed fine; the managed approuter can’t route to it. Check these:

  1. xs-app.json must be inside webapp/ (so it’s in the zip) and have a catch-all route ^(.*)$ → html5-apps-repo-rt with authenticationType: xsuaa.
  2. MTA destination content needs both the repo-host destination and an XSUAA destination (OAuth2UserTokenExchange), each with sap.cloud.service: hrformulieren. A missing UAA destination causes exactly this 404.
  3. manifest.json needs "sap.cloud": { "public": true, "service": "hrformulieren" }, or the inbox can’t load it.
  4. URL format: https://<subdomain>.launchpad.cfapps.<region>.hana.ondemand.com/hrformulieren.hrformulieren/manifest.json
  5. Work Zone subscription must be active in the same subaccount.

entry.title: How to Integrate an AI Assistant into an SAP Transaction Using ABAP AI tools
entry.content:
How to Integrate an AI Assistant into an SAP Transaction Using ABAP AI tools

 

 

 

 

 

 

Here, we will walk through a step-by-step implementation of an AI Assistant in the BP transaction using ABAP AI tools, along with the building blocks required for this integration.

We will use the BP transaction because it is available in SAP ABAP trial systems. This makes the example useful for ABAP developers who use trial systems to learn and experiment.

General Technical Prerequisites

As with any custom development within a standard SAP transaction, integrating an AI Assistant requires an appropriate enhancement or extension mechanism, such as a BAdI, a user exit, or another supported enhancement option.

Ideally, users should be able to open the AI Assistant on demand. To achieve this, the SAP transaction must provide a way to customize its user interface, allowing us to add an entry point for the Assistant. This could be a menu option, a screen element, or another interactive UI component, depending on the extension options available in the transaction.

Some SAP transactions provide specific mechanisms for customizing or extending their user interfaces. The BP transaction is a good example, as it uses the Business Data Toolset (BDT), a central framework for configuring and extending Business Partner (BP) maintenance screens, dialog programs, and transactions without modifying standard SAP source code.

Other standard transactions may not provide a supported way to add custom menus or screen elements. In such cases, it may still be possible to open the AI Assistant automatically when the transaction starts. To achieve this, we need to identify an appropriate enhancement option, such as a BAdI or user exit, that is triggered at a suitable point during the transaction's execution and allows the Assistant to be launched.

The key takeaway is that we need to analyze each standard transaction to determine the available options for integrating the AI Assistant, whether through a user interface enhancement or an alternative mechanism.

ABAP AI tools Prerequisites

This example requires both ABAP AI tools and ABAP AI tools User Interface to be installed on your system.

For the ABAP AI tools installation, see: https://github.com/christianjianelli/yaai

For the ABAP AI tools User Interface installation, see: https://github.com/christianjianelli/yaai_ui

The Business Partner AI Assistant

For the AI Assistant's user interface, we will use the ABAP AI tools User Interface to provide the chat interface through which users can interact with the Assistant.

To implement the AI Assistant itself, we will use ABAP AI tools, providing system instructions and tools.

Extending the Business Partner Transaction

For this example, we are going to configure a custom event that will be available in the Extras → More Extras menu in the BP transaction. We will use this custom event to provide users with a way to open the AI Assistant chat.

The steps are as follows:

1. Create a function group, for example, ZFG_AAI_BP.

2. In this function group, create a function module with the same parameters as the standard function module BUA_BUPA_EVENT_FCODE. For example, Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI. The function code YAAI will be used to instantiate the AI Assistant chat.

FUNCTION Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI
  IMPORTING
    VALUE(I_FCODE) LIKE TBZ4-FCODE OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSFIELD) LIKE BUS000TBFL-TBFLD OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSLINE) LIKE SY-LILLI OPTIONAL
  EXPORTING
    VALUE(E_XHANDLE) TYPE C.



  e_xhandle = 'X'.

  IF i_fcode <> 'YAAI'.

    CLEAR e_xhandle.

    RETURN.

  ENDIF.

ENDFUNCTION.

3. Open transaction BUS9 and choose New Entries to create a new function code. Set the function code to YAAI and enter AI Assistant as the function text.

Keep the Active by Activity, View, and Sequence Category option selected, and enter 4 (Extras) in the Menu field. Select all checkboxes under Save Mode and Transfer Mode.

Next, double-click Active In Each View on the left, choose New Entries, leave the View field empty, and select all checkboxes under Save Mode and Transfer Mode.

Then, double-click Active In Each View/Screen Sequence Category, choose New Entries, leave the View and Screen Sequence Category fields empty, and select all checkboxes under Save Mode and Transfer Mode.

 

 

 

4. Open transaction BUS7, select the FCODE entry, and then double-click Event → Function Modules. Choose New Entries and enter 9000001 in the Item field. Enter the name of the function module you created, Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI, select X in the Call field, and enter BUP in the Application field.

 

 

After completing these steps, you should see AI Assistant in the Extras → More Extras menu.

 

Implementing the Instantiation of the Chat User Interface

Let's now implement the instantiation of the chat user interface through which users will interact with the AI Assistant.

For now, we will implement only the minimum code required to display the chat. Later, we will provide system instructions and tools to the AI Assistant.

FUNCTION Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI
  IMPORTING
    VALUE(I_FCODE) LIKE TBZ4-FCODE OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSFIELD) LIKE BUS000TBFL-TBFLD OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSLINE) LIKE SY-LILLI OPTIONAL
  EXPORTING
    VALUE(E_XHANDLE) TYPE C.



  e_xhandle = 'X'.

  IF i_fcode <> 'YAAI'.

    CLEAR e_xhandle.

    RETURN.

  ENDIF.

  IF o_chat IS BOUND.

    o_chat->display( ).

    RETURN.

  ENDIF.

  DATA(lo_openai) = NEW ycl_aai_openai( ).

  o_chat = NEW #( io_api = lo_openai
                  i_greeting = 'How can I help you today?' ).

  o_chat->display( ).

ENDFUNCTION.

Now that the instantiation is implemented, clicking the AI Assistant in the Extras → More Extras menu should display the AI Assistant Chat on the right side of the screen, as illustrated in the following screenshot.

 

At this point, the AI Assistant would be able to help users by answering their questions, but it would not have instructions or context beyond what the user might provide.

Implementing the Tools

Interacting with an LLM (Large Language Model) directly within an SAP transaction is useful, but we can achieve much more. By providing tools, we can enable the LLM to interact directly with the system, access contextual information, and perform actions on behalf of the user.

For this example, we will keep the implementation simple by creating tools that allow the AI Assistant to retrieve information about the current context of the BP transaction. Specifically, the context will include the validation messages displayed to the user when they attempt to save changes, as well as some basic information about the Business Partner being edited.

BP Transaction Context

To provide contextual information to the AI Assistant, we need to collect and store it in memory. For this example, we will create a class named ZCL_BP_CONTEXT to store the context using static attributes. This will allow us to retrieve this information later using the tools that we will create.

Create a class named ZCL_BP_CONTEXT with the following code:

CLASS zcl_bp_context DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    CONSTANTS mc_msgid TYPE bapiret2-id VALUE 'ZBP' ##NO_TEXT.

    CLASS-DATA: mt_messages TYPE bapiret2_t READ-ONLY.

    CLASS-DATA: ms_but000  TYPE but000 READ-ONLY,
                ms_address TYPE bapibus1006_address READ-ONLY.

    CLASS-METHODS set_data
      IMPORTING
        i_s_but000  TYPE but000 OPTIONAL
        i_s_address TYPE bapibus1006_address OPTIONAL.

    CLASS-METHODS add_message
      IMPORTING
        i_s_msg TYPE bapiret2.

    CLASS-METHODS add_messages
      IMPORTING
        i_t_msg TYPE bapiret2_t.

    CLASS-METHODS reset.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_bp_context IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD set_data.

    IF i_s_but000 IS SUPPLIED.
      ms_but000 = i_s_but000.
    ENDIF.

    IF i_s_address IS SUPPLIED.
      ms_address = i_s_address.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD add_message.

    IF i_s_msg-number IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(ls_msg) = i_s_msg.

    IF ls_msg-id IS INITIAL.
      ls_msg-id = mc_msgid.
    ENDIF.

    IF ls_msg-type IS INITIAL.
      ls_msg-type = 'E' ##NO_TEXT.
    ENDIF.

    " If it is a SAP standard error message, then we need to discard all other messages
    " because the system doesn't call all BAdIs when standard validations fail, and
    " consequently, we are not able to update the context accordingly.
    IF ls_msg-type = 'E' AND ls_msg-id(1) <> 'Z' .

      FREE mt_messages.

      APPEND ls_msg TO mt_messages.

    ELSE.

      READ TABLE mt_messages TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS
        WITH KEY
          id = ls_msg-id
          type = ls_msg-type
          number = ls_msg-number
          message_v1 = ls_msg-message_v1
          message_v2 = ls_msg-message_v2
          message_v3 = ls_msg-message_v3
          message_v4 = ls_msg-message_v4.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND ls_msg TO mt_messages.
      ENDIF.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD add_messages.

    " Discard messages from previous check
    IF i_t_msg IS NOT INITIAL AND i_t_msg[ 1 ]-parameter IS NOT INITIAL.

      DELETE mt_messages WHERE parameter = i_t_msg[ 1 ]-parameter.

    ENDIF.

    LOOP AT i_t_msg ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_message>).

      add_message( <ls_message> ).

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD reset.

    FREE mt_messages.

    CLEAR: ms_but000,
           ms_address.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

BP Transaction Context Tools

Now that we have the class that will hold the contextual information in memory, let's implement the tools that will provide it to the AI Assistant.

Create a class named ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS with the following code:

CLASS zcl_bp_context_tools DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    METHODS get_bp_basic_info
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS get_messages
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_bp_context_tools IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_bp_basic_info.

    r_response = space.

    IF zcl_bp_context=>ms_but000 IS INITIAL.

      r_response = |No information available. Instruct the user to execute the check on the BP transaction|.
      r_response = |{ r_response } using either the Check button or the F8 key.|.

      RETURN.

    ENDIF.

    r_response = |Partner: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_but000-partner ALPHA = OUT }|.
    r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }First Name: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_but000-name_first }|.
    r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Last Name: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_but000-name_last }|.

    IF zcl_bp_context=>ms_address IS NOT INITIAL.

      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }BP Address|.
      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Street: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_address-street }|.
      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Number: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_address-house_no }|.
      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }City: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_address-city }|.
      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Postal Code: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_address-postl_cod1 }|.
      r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Country: { zcl_bp_context=>ms_address-country }|.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_messages.

    FREE r_response.

    LOOP AT zcl_bp_context=>mt_messages ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_message>).

      MESSAGE ID <ls_message>-id
                TYPE <ls_message>-type
                NUMBER <ls_message>-number
                WITH <ls_message>-message_v1
                     <ls_message>-message_v2
                     <ls_message>-message_v3
                     <ls_message>-message_v4
                INTO DATA(l_message_text).

      IF r_response IS INITIAL.

        r_response = |Messages:{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Type: '{ <ls_message>-type }' Text: { l_message_text }|.

      ELSE.

        r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }Type: '{ <ls_message>-type }' Text: { l_message_text }|.

      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

Collecting the Contextual Information in the BP Transaction

To collect contextual information from the BP transaction, we will implement the BAdIs BUPA_ADDR_CHECK and BUPA_FURTHER_CHECKS. Within the BUPA_ADDR_CHECK BAdI, we will implement validations and store the resulting messages in the BP context class ZCL_BP_CONTEXT. Additionally, we will store BP information in the context class within both BAdIs.

Implement the BAdIs and add the following code to their methods.

BAdI BUPA_ADDR_CHECK

Note: For the postal code validation used in this BAdI, it is necessary to have the postal code field length correctly set in transaction OY17.

 

 

CLASS zcl_im_bupa_addr_check DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    INTERFACES if_ex_bupa_addr_check .
  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_im_bupa_addr_check IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD if_ex_bupa_addr_check~check.

    CONSTANTS: lc_msgid     TYPE bapiret2-id VALUE 'ZBP',
               lc_parameter TYPE bapiret2-parameter VALUE 'BUPA_ADDR_CHECK'.

    DATA: l_post_code TYPE string,
          l_city      TYPE string,
          l_prefix    TYPE string.


    IF is_address IS NOT INITIAL.

      " Add BP info to the context
      zcl_bp_context=>set_data(
        EXPORTING
          i_s_address = is_address
      ).

    ENDIF.

    IF is_address-postl_cod1 IS NOT INITIAL AND is_address-country = 'PT'.

      l_post_code = |{ is_address-postl_cod1 }|.
      l_city = to_upper( condense( is_address-city ) ).

      " 1. Validate the postal code format
      IF l_post_code IS INITIAL OR
         strlen( l_post_code ) <> 8 OR
         l_post_code+4(1) <> '-'.

        " The postal code must have the format NNNN-NNN
        APPEND VALUE #( id = lc_msgid
                        number = '001'
                        type = 'E'
                        parameter = lc_parameter ) TO et_return.

      ELSE.

        " Check that the remaining characters are numeric
        DATA(l_digits) = l_post_code(4) && l_post_code+5(3).

        IF NOT l_digits CO '0123456789' OR strlen( condense( l_digits ) ) <> 7.

          " The postal code must contain seven digits
          APPEND VALUE #( id = lc_msgid
                          number = '002'
                          type = 'E'
                          parameter = lc_parameter ) TO et_return.

        ELSE.

          " 2. Extract the first four digits
          l_prefix = l_post_code(4).

          CASE l_city.

            WHEN 'LISBON' OR 'LISBOA'.

              IF l_prefix(1) <> '1'.

                " The postal code prefix is inconsistent with Lisbon
                APPEND VALUE #( id = lc_msgid
                                number = '003'
                                type = 'E'
                                message_v1 = is_address-city
                                parameter = lc_parameter ) TO et_return.

              ENDIF.

            WHEN 'PORTO'.

              IF l_prefix(1) <> '4'.

                " The postal code prefix is inconsistent with Porto
                APPEND VALUE #( id = lc_msgid
                                number = '003'
                                type = 'E'
                                message_v1 = is_address-city
                                parameter = lc_parameter ) TO et_return.

              ENDIF.

            WHEN OTHERS.
              " No city/prefix rule defined for this city

          ENDCASE.

        ENDIF.

      ENDIF.

    ENDIF.

    IF is_address IS NOT INITIAL AND et_return[] IS INITIAL.

      " Personal address data of business partner is error-free.
      APPEND VALUE #( id = lc_msgid
                      number = '004'
                      type = 'S'
                      parameter = lc_parameter ) TO et_return.

    ENDIF.

    " Add messages to the context
    zcl_bp_context=>add_messages( et_return ).

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

 

Message class ZBP

 

BAdI BUPA_FURTHER_CHECKS

CLASS zcl_im_bupa_further_checks DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    INTERFACES if_ex_bupa_further_checks.

  PROTECTED SECTION.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_im_bupa_further_checks IMPLEMENTATION.


  METHOD if_ex_bupa_further_checks~check_central.

    IF ( sy-msgid IS NOT INITIAL AND
         sy-msgno IS NOT INITIAL AND
         sy-msgty IS NOT INITIAL ) AND
       ( sy-msgid <> 'R11' AND
         sy-msgno <> '555' AND
         sy-msgv1 <> '000000' ).



      zcl_bp_context=>add_messages( VALUE #( ( id = sy-msgid
                                               number = sy-msgno
                                               type = sy-msgty
                                               message_v1 = sy-msgv1
                                               message_v2 = sy-msgv2
                                               message_v3 = sy-msgv3
                                               message_v4 = sy-msgv4
                                               parameter  = sy-tcode ) ) ).

    ENDIF.

    " Add BP basic info to the context
    zcl_bp_context=>set_data(
      EXPORTING
        i_s_but000 = is_but000
    ).



  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

Providing System Instructions and Tools to the AI Assistant

Let's now provide our AI Assistant with system instructions and tools.

Edit the function module Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI and update it with the following code.

FUNCTION Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI
  IMPORTING
    VALUE(I_FCODE) LIKE TBZ4-FCODE OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSFIELD) LIKE BUS000TBFL-TBFLD OPTIONAL
    VALUE(I_CRSLINE) LIKE SY-LILLI OPTIONAL
  EXPORTING
    VALUE(E_XHANDLE) TYPE C.



  e_xhandle = 'X'.

  IF i_fcode <> 'YAAI'.

    CLEAR e_xhandle.

    RETURN.

  ENDIF.

  IF o_chat IS BOUND.

    o_chat->display( ).

    RETURN.

  ENDIF.

  DATA l_instructions TYPE string.

  DATA(l_newline) = cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline.

  l_instructions = |# Role and Purpose{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }You are an AI Assistant integrated into the SAP Business Partner (BP) transaction.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Your primary purpose is to help users understand and work with the BP transaction,{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }answer questions related to Business Partner data,{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }and provide guidance based on the context of the current transaction.{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }You should act as a knowledgeable, practical, and helpful assistant for SAP users.{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }# Available Tools and Transaction Context{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }You have access to tools that can retrieve information about the current execution{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }context of the BP transaction.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Use these tools whenever the user's question requires information about{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }the current transaction or Business Partner.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Do not assume that you already know the current Business Partner's data or{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }the messages generated during transaction execution.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Retrieve the relevant information through the available tools when necessary.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Only use information returned by the tools or explicitly provided by the user{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }when answering questions about the current transaction context.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Instruct the user to click the Check button in the BP transaction.|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }This action is required to update the contextual information used by the tools.{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }# Scope{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Focus primarily on questions related to the SAP Business Partner transaction and{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }the context made available through your tools.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }If a question is unrelated to this scope, briefly explain your primary purpose and, when appropriate, { l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }help the user formulate a question related to the Business Partner transaction.{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }# Communication Style{ l_newline }|.

  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }Use professional, friendly, and straightforward language.{ l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }When appropriate, provide step-by-step instructions to help users resolve issues or { l_newline }|.
  l_instructions = |{ l_instructions }understand the information displayed in the BP transaction.|.


  DATA(lo_openai) = NEW ycl_aai_openai( ).

  lo_openai->set_system_instructions( l_instructions ).

  DATA(lo_function_calling) = NEW ycl_aai_func_call_openai( ).

  lo_function_calling->add_methods( VALUE #( ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_BP_BASIC_INFO'
                                               description = 'Use this method to retrieve the basic information of the Business Partner being edited/viewed by the user.' )

                                             ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_MESSAGES'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the messages displayed to the user in the BP transaction.' ) ) ).

  lo_openai->bind_tools( lo_function_calling ).

  o_chat = NEW #( io_api = lo_openai
                  i_greeting = 'How can I help you today?' ).

  o_chat->display( ).

ENDFUNCTION.

At this point, the AI Assistant would be able to answer users' questions, follow the instructions, and retrieve contextual information about the Business Partner being edited in the BP transaction using the provided tools.

Let's test it.

 

What Have We Developed So Far?

Let's stop for a moment and look at how this works under the hood. An image may be worth a thousand words, so let's visualize the architecture in a diagram.

 

Equipping the AI Assistant to Perform Actions on the User's Behalf

Let's now create a tool that allows the AI Assistant to make changes to the personal address of the Business Partner being edited in the BP transaction.

Create a class named ZCL_BUPA_PERSON_ADDRESS_TOOLS with the following code:

CLASS zcl_bupa_person_address_tools DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_addr2_data_subset_s,
             street     TYPE addr2_data-street,
             house_num1 TYPE addr2_data-house_num1,
             house_num2 TYPE addr2_data-house_num2,
             city1      TYPE addr2_data-city1,
             post_code1 TYPE addr2_data-post_code1,
             country    TYPE addr2_data-country,
           END OF ty_addr2_data_subset_s.

    METHODS read_bupa_address_from_screen
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS update_bupa_address_on_screen
      IMPORTING
                i_street          TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-street
                i_house_num1      TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-house_num1
                i_house_num2      TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-house_num2
                i_city            TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-city
                i_post_code       TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-post_code
                i_country         TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-country
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS read_bupa_address_from_memory
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS update_bupa_address_in_memory
      IMPORTING
                i_street          TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-street
                i_house_num1      TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-house_num1
                i_house_num2      TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-house_num2
                i_city            TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-city
                i_post_code       TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-post_code
                i_country         TYPE zst_bupa_address_tool-country
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.

  PRIVATE SECTION.

    METHODS _get_bupa_address_from_memory
      EXPORTING
        e_s_address_value     TYPE addr2_val
        e_s_address_selection TYPE addr2_sel.

ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_bupa_person_address_tools IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD read_bupa_address_from_memory.

    FREE r_response.

    me->_get_bupa_address_from_memory(
      IMPORTING
        e_s_address_value = DATA(ls_address_personal_value)
    ).

    DATA(ls_bupa_address) = VALUE zst_bupa_address_tool( street      = ls_address_personal_value-street
                                                         house_num1  = ls_address_personal_value-house_num1
                                                         house_num2  = ls_address_personal_value-house_num2
                                                         city        = ls_address_personal_value-city1
                                                         post_code   = ls_address_personal_value-post_code1
                                                         country     = ls_address_personal_value-country ).

    IF ls_bupa_address IS NOT INITIAL.
      r_response = /ui2/cl_json=>serialize( data = ls_bupa_address ).
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD read_bupa_address_from_screen.

    FREE r_response.

    ASSIGN ('(SAPLSZA7)ADDR2_DATA') TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<addr2_data>).

    IF <addr2_data> IS NOT ASSIGNED OR <addr2_data> IS INITIAL.
      r_response = 'Business Partner address is not available.'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(ls_addr2_data_subset) = CORRESPONDING ty_addr2_data_subset_s( <addr2_data> ).

    DATA(ls_bupa_address) = VALUE zst_bupa_address_tool( street     = ls_addr2_data_subset-street
                                                         house_num1 = ls_addr2_data_subset-house_num1
                                                         house_num2 = ls_addr2_data_subset-house_num2
                                                         city       = ls_addr2_data_subset-city1
                                                         post_code  = ls_addr2_data_subset-post_code1
                                                         country    = ls_addr2_data_subset-country ).

    IF ls_bupa_address IS NOT INITIAL.
      r_response = /ui2/cl_json=>serialize( data = ls_bupa_address ).
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD update_bupa_address_on_screen.

    FREE r_response.

    ASSIGN ('(SAPLSZA7)ADDR2_DATA') TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<addr2_data>).

    IF <addr2_data> IS ASSIGNED.

      DATA(lo_aai_util) = NEW ycl_aai_util( ).

      DATA(ls_addr2_subset) = VALUE ty_addr2_data_subset_s( street = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_street ) )
                                                            house_num1 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_house_num1 ) )
                                                            house_num2 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_house_num2 ) )
                                                            city1 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_city ) )
                                                            post_code1 = i_post_code
                                                            country = i_country ).

      <addr2_data> = CORRESPONDING #( ls_addr2_subset ).

    ELSE.
      r_response = 'Error while updating the Business Partner address on screen.'.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD update_bupa_address_in_memory.

    DATA ls_address_personal_data TYPE addr2_data.

    FREE r_response.

    me->_get_bupa_address_from_memory(
      IMPORTING
        e_s_address_value = DATA(ls_address_personal_value)
        e_s_address_selection = DATA(ls_address_personal_selection)
    ).

    IF ls_address_personal_value IS INITIAL.
      r_response = 'Business Partner address is not available in memory.'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    ls_address_personal_data = CORRESPONDING #( ls_address_personal_value ).

    DATA(lo_aai_util) = NEW ycl_aai_util( ).

    ls_address_personal_data-street = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_street ) ).
    ls_address_personal_data-house_num1 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_house_num1 ) ).
    ls_address_personal_data-house_num2 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_house_num2 ) ).
    ls_address_personal_data-city1 = lo_aai_util->replace_unicode_escape_seq( CONV #( i_city ) ).
    ls_address_personal_data-post_code1 = i_post_code.
    ls_address_personal_data-country = i_country.

    CALL FUNCTION 'ADDR_PERSONAL_UPDATE'
      EXPORTING
        address_handle             = ls_address_personal_selection-addrhandle
        address_number             = ls_address_personal_selection-addrnumber
        address_personal_data      = ls_address_personal_data
        language                   = sy-langu
        nation                     = ls_address_personal_selection-nation
        person_handle              = ls_address_personal_selection-pershandle
        person_number              = ls_address_personal_selection-persnumber
        check_address              = space
      EXCEPTIONS
        parameter_error            = 1
        personal_address_not_exist = 2
        version_not_exist          = 3
        internal_error             = 4
        OTHERS                     = 99.

    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      r_response = 'Business Partner address was updated.'.
    ELSE.
      r_response = 'Business Partner address update failed.'.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD _get_bupa_address_from_memory.

    DATA l_field TYPE string.

    DATA: ls_address_personal_selection TYPE addr2_sel,
          ls_address_personal_value     TYPE addr2_val.

    CLEAR: e_s_address_value,
           e_s_address_selection.

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_PERSON_NUMBER'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_person_number>).

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_ADDRESS_NUMBER'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_address_number>).

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_PERSON_HANDLE'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_person_handle>).

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_ADDRESS_HANDLE'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_address_handle>).

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_NATION'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_nation>).

    l_field = '(SAPLSZA7)G_DATE_FROM'.
    ASSIGN (l_field) TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<g_date_from>).

    IF <g_person_number> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-persnumber = <g_person_number>.
    ENDIF.

    IF <g_address_number> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-addrnumber = <g_address_number>.
    ENDIF.

    IF <g_person_handle> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-pershandle = <g_person_handle>.
    ENDIF.

    IF <g_address_handle> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-addrhandle = <g_address_handle>.
    ENDIF.

    IF <g_nation> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-nation = <g_nation>.
    ENDIF.

    IF <g_date_from> IS ASSIGNED.
      ls_address_personal_selection-date = <g_date_from>.
    ENDIF.

    IF ls_address_personal_selection IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    CALL FUNCTION 'ADDR_PERSONAL_GET'
      EXPORTING
        address_personal_selection = ls_address_personal_selection
        iv_current_comm_data       = abap_true
      IMPORTING
        address_personal_value     = ls_address_personal_value
      EXCEPTIONS
        parameter_error            = 1
        address_not_exist          = 2
        person_not_exist           = 3
        version_not_exist          = 4
        internal_error             = 5
        OTHERS                     = 6.

    e_s_address_value = ls_address_personal_value.
    e_s_address_selection = ls_address_personal_selection.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

After implementing the tools, edit the function module Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI to add the new tools.

Replace this part of the code:

  lo_function_calling->add_methods( VALUE #( ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_BP_BASIC_INFO'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the basic information of the Business Partner being edited by the user.' )

                                             ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_MESSAGES'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the messages displayed to the user in the BP transaction.' ) ) ).

With this:

  lo_function_calling->add_methods( VALUE #( ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_BP_BASIC_INFO'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the basic information of the Business Partner being edited/viewed by the user.' )

                                             ( class_name = 'ZCL_BP_CONTEXT_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'GET_MESSAGES'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the messages displayed to the user in the BP transaction.' )

                                             ( class_name = 'ZCL_BUPA_PERSON_ADDRESS_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'READ_BUPA_ADDRESS_FROM_MEMORY'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to retrieve the personal address data of the Business Partner being edited by the user.' )

                                             ( class_name = 'ZCL_BUPA_PERSON_ADDRESS_TOOLS'
                                               method_name = 'UPDATE_BUPA_ADDRESS_IN_MEMORY'
                                               description = 'Use this tool to update the personal address data of the Business Partner being edited by the user.' ) ) ).

With these new tools, the AI Assistant can update the personal address of a Business Partner within the BP transaction. Note that the tool changes the current address data stored in memory. This is one of the most useful capabilities of this type of integration: because the tool runs in the same internal session as the SAP transaction, it can access the current data stored in memory, provided, of course, that the transaction allows the data to be referenced or retrieved.

Let's test it.

 

As you can see, by providing tools, we can extend the AI Assistant’s capabilities and make it more useful to users. Since these tools are implemented in ABAP, we can do virtually anything ABAP can do in this context.

Let’s explore a few more examples of tools.

The class cl_gui_frontend_services provides some useful features that we can utilize to extend the AI assistant's capabilities.

  • Screenshot Tool — The get_screenshot method can be used to capture screenshots and send them back to the assistant.
  • Clipboard Tools — The clipboard_import and clipboard_export methods allow the assistant to access the user's clipboard, enabling it to read and write clipboard data.

Here is the class that implements these tools.

CLASS zcl_aai_gui_tools DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC .

  PUBLIC SECTION.

    TYPES ty_row TYPE c LENGTH 262143.

    METHODS get_screenshot
      EXPORTING
                e_t_files         TYPE ytt_aai_files
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS set_clipboard_data
      IMPORTING
                i_clipboard_data  TYPE string
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

    METHODS get_clipboard_data
      RETURNING VALUE(r_response) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.



CLASS zcl_aai_gui_tools IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD get_screenshot.

    DATA: l_mime_type      TYPE string,
          l_file_extension TYPE string,
          l_image          TYPE xstring.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>get_screenshot(
      IMPORTING
        mime_type_str        = l_mime_type
        image                = l_image
      EXCEPTIONS
        access_denied        = 1
        cntl_error           = 2
        error_no_gui         = 3
        not_supported_by_gui = 4
        OTHERS               = 5
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.

      IF sy-subrc = 1.
        r_response = 'Error: access denied.'.
      ELSE.
        r_response = 'An error occurred while generating screenshot.'.
      ENDIF.

    ELSE.

      r_response = 'Here is the requested screenshot.'.

      SPLIT l_mime_type AT '/' INTO DATA(l_dummy) l_file_extension.

      IF l_file_extension IS NOT INITIAL.
        l_file_extension = condense( '.' && l_file_extension ).
      ENDIF.

      e_t_files = VALUE #( ( content = cl_http_utility=>encode_x_base64( unencoded = l_image )
                             filename = |screenshot{ l_file_extension }|
                             file_size = xstrlen( l_image )
                             file_type = l_mime_type ) ).

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_clipboard_data.

    DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>clipboard_import(
      IMPORTING
        data                 = lt_data
        length               = DATA(l_length)
      EXCEPTIONS
        cntl_error           = 1                " Control error
        error_no_gui         = 2                " No GUI available
        not_supported_by_gui = 3                " GUI does not support this
        OTHERS               = 4
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.

      r_response = 'Error while importing data from the clipboard.'.

    ELSE.

      IF lt_data IS INITIAL.
        r_response = 'The clipboard is empty.'.
      ENDIF.

      LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<l_row>).

        IF r_response IS INITIAL.
          r_response = <l_row>.
        ELSE.
          r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }{ <l_row> }|.
        ENDIF.

      ENDLOOP.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD set_clipboard_data.

    DATA lt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_row.

    DATA l_rc TYPE i.

    SPLIT i_clipboard_data AT cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline INTO TABLE lt_data.

    cl_gui_frontend_services=>clipboard_export(
      IMPORTING
        data                 = lt_data                 " Data
      CHANGING
        rc                   = l_rc                 " Return Code
      EXCEPTIONS
        cntl_error           = 1                " Control error
        error_no_gui         = 2                " No GUI available
        not_supported_by_gui = 3                " GUI does not support this
        no_authority         = 4                " Authorization check failed
        OTHERS               = 5
    ).

    IF sy-subrc <> 0 OR l_rc <> 0.

      r_response = 'Error while exporting data to the clipboard.'.

    ELSE.

      LOOP AT lt_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<l_row>).

        IF r_response IS INITIAL.
          r_response = <l_row>.
        ELSE.
          r_response = |{ r_response }{ cl_abap_char_utilities=>newline }{ <l_row> }|.
        ENDIF.

      ENDLOOP.

    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

In case you want to test these tools, edit the function module Z_F_EVENT_FCODE_YAAI and update its code by adding them in the lo_function_calling->add_methods method call, similarly to what we did when we added the Personal Address tools.

Other examples of tools you can build:

  • Call a transaction, similar to a drill-down report.
  • Perform background tasks.
  • Read, write, upload, and download files.
  • Send emails.
  • ... and certainly many, many more! 🙂

A System-Wide Entry Point: Adding the AI Assistant to MENUSYST

As discussed in the General Technical Prerequisites section, adding an entry point for the AI Assistant usually means finding a suitable enhancement for each transaction. There is another option: adding an item to the SAP standard system menu, MENUSYST, to provide a common way to launch the Assistant across transactions, without enhancing each transaction’s user interface individually.

I'm generally opposed to modifying SAP standard objects. I would consider it only in very exceptional cases and only when the change poses no risk to the system’s existing functionality. This approach does involve a standard-system change, which may require minor adjustments during upgrades.

The required changes are:

Transaction: SE41

Program: MENUSYST

Status: MEN

 

 

Transaction: SE37

Function Module: HELP_START

 

With this approach, we can provide a system-wide entry point that determines whether the AI Assistant can be launched in the current transaction and, if so, which assistant to instantiate, along with the appropriate system instructions and tools.

 

 

Closing Thoughts

That's it for this post! I hope the ideas and examples shared here give you a good starting point for integrating AI assistants into your SAP system.

There are many ways to approach this, and the right solution will depend on the transactions you want to enhance and the extension options available in your SAP environment.

I'd love to hear about your experiences, what you build, and what you learn along the way.

entry.title: Re: Theme issues in Personas SP19
entry.content:
That’s usually a Personas Theme (or flavor-level CSS) that isn’t applied or is being overridden in SP19.

What to check:

  1. Personas Theme assignment: in /PERSONAS/ADMIN (or the Personas theme editor), check whether a Personas Theme was assigned to EWM_MOBGUI / /SCWM/RFUI, and whether it’s still active and assigned after the upgrade. If it was, reopen it in the SP19 editor and re-save it.
  2. Pin the base theme: test with &sap-theme=sap_belize (or whichever theme you used before) on the same URL. If the white background and blue borders come back, add that theme as a GUI configuration parameter on EWM_MOBGUI in SICF so it no longer follows the new Horizon default.
  3. Isolate Personas: test with &sap-personas-runmode=0. If the plain MOBGUI also shows the grey background, the base theme is the cause (step 2). If not, it’s the Personas theme or flavor (step 1).
  4. Flavor CSS: if the borders and bold font were set in the flavor (style properties or a custom CSS script), SP19 may now render them with different control classes. Edit one button in the flavor editor and see whether the border and font settings are still there.

entry.title: From Hard-Coded Values to Maintainable SAP Solutions
entry.content:
During an SAP remediation project, I encountered a challenge that made me think differently about how we manage changing business requirements in custom ABAP programs.

An organizational structure reassignment meant that existing organizational values needed to change across multiple custom programs. At first, this looked like a straightforward task: identify the old values and replace them with the new ones.

But there was a bigger question to consider.

If these values change again in the future, should we have to revisit the source code of multiple programs every time?

Instead of simply replacing one hard-coded value with another, our approach was to externalize the values into a KTern HLR (Hard-coded Literal Remediation) configuration table.

This experience got me thinking about a broader development principle: solving the immediate requirement is important, but designing for the next change matters too.

Moving Organizational Values Out of the Source Code

In our project, the hard-coded literals being remediated included organizational values such as company codes and sales-area-related values. These values were embedded in multiple custom ABAP programs, meaning that an organizational change could require updates across different source-code locations.

The approach involved a KTern HLR configuration table. Instead of keeping the relevant values directly in the source code, we externalized them into a custom ZTAB_* table.

A custom ZCL_* ABAP class retrieved the required configuration at runtime using the combination of PROGNAME and CONTEXTID.

The distinction was simple: the table stored the values, while the class handled retrieving the relevant entry for the program and context.

This separated the values from the program logic and provided a way to maintain them independently of the source code.

Why This Matters Beyond One Remediation Project

The main benefit of this approach is not simply that hard-coded values are moved into a table. It is that future maintenance can become more manageable.

When an organizational value changes, the team can update the relevant configuration entry instead of modifying every program that uses it—provided the existing implementation supports that change.

It also makes the design easier to reason about. The value is maintained in a defined location, and the program retrieves it through an established mechanism rather than relying on a literal embedded in the code.

However, this approach is not a universal replacement for hard-coding. Some values are stable technical constants, while others represent business configuration that may change over time. Those cases should be evaluated differently.

Externalizing a value also introduces responsibilities. Configuration entries must be maintained correctly, the runtime lookup must handle missing or invalid entries, and changes must be tested to confirm that the program still behaves as expected.

Moving a value out of the code helps only when the surrounding design makes that value safe and meaningful to maintain.

What I Took Away From This Experience

Working on this remediation made me look beyond the immediate code change.

A solution can meet today's requirement and still leave the same maintenance problem waiting for the next organizational change. Thinking about where changeable values belong—and how programs should retrieve them—can make a meaningful difference to the long-term maintainability of custom SAP solutions.

For me, the lesson was straightforward: don't just ask how to replace a hard-coded value. Ask whether that value should have been embedded in the code in the first place.

FAQ 8 questions

Do I need Joule to use the Second Brain? ▾
Yes — the initialization wizard runs inside SAP Joule Work (or any Claude Code-compatible AI). Once your vault is set up, you also use Joule as the AI that reads and writes to your vault during daily work. The vault itself is just a folder on your local machine.
 
What happens to my data — is it sent to the cloud? ▾
Your vault files live on your local machine. During a Joule session the AI reads the files you open as context, but the files themselves are never uploaded or stored externally. Follow standard SAP data protection guidelines (DPP) for what you share with AI tools — in particular, do not record or share content from meetings with external parties (customers, partners).
 
How long does the initial setup take? ▾
The 9-step wizard takes approximately 10–15 minutes. The AI creates all folders and deploys all skills automatically — you only answer questions and confirm choices. Once done your vault is immediately usable.
 
Can I use the vault for non-HANA topics? ▾
Yes. The vault is role-specific but topic-agnostic. It can hold SAP Notes, BTP documentation, S/4HANA content, meeting notes, emails, and any other artifact you want to distil and retrieve. How do I update a note when the source document changes? ▾
Drop the updated source into 00_Inbox and run the intake skill. The AI distils the new version and updates the last_reviewed timestamp. For SAP Notes it diffs against the existing note and appends new content only, preserving your existing annotations.
 
Can I share my vault with a colleague? ▾
You can share individual distilled notes (as .md files) and the offline HTML boards. Do not share the full vault folder externally — it may contain customer-confidential content in 05_Cases/. Use the confidentiality-scrub skill before sharing any content outside SAP.
 
What is the "0 fabricated" standard? ▾
Every distilled note from a verified source carries a declaration: "0 fabricated — all content verified against the source document." SAP Note numbers, parameter names, and view names are copied verbatim from the source — the AI never infers or invents them. This is the trust property that makes distilled notes usable in customer communications and escalation discussions.
 
How is this different from SAP's standard Joule features? ▾
Standard Joule answers questions from its training data. Your Second Brain adds your personal knowledge: cases you worked, SAP Notes you read, whiteboards you drew, customer situations you resolved. The AI then answers from your expertise — not generic SAP documentation. The vault is the difference between a fresh Joule session and an expert-calibrated Joule session.

entry.title: Welcome Back: Smarter, Faster Rehire in SAP SuccessFactors Onboarding 2H 2026
entry.content:
Bringing People Back Has Never Been Easier - Rehire Enhancements 2H 2026 Release 

When a former employee decides to come back, that decision says something important about your organization. They know the culture, they have the context, and from day one they can contribute in ways that a brand-new hire takes months to reach. The rehire journey should match that level of confidence. 

Across this release, we focused on making every step of the rehire experience faster, more accurate, and less dependent on manual intervention. These enhancements were shaped by direct customer feedback — from organizations running thousands of rehires a year who told us exactly where they needed the system to work harder for them. Here is everything that is new. 

 

Smarter Hire-Type Routing for Returning Employees 

Feature: Rehire on New Employment with Future Termination 

Customers asked us to make hire-type classification more accurate for returning employees whose termination dates had already been scheduled in advance. We delivered a solution that removes ambiguity entirely. 

When a rehire is initiated — through SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting, a third-party applicant tracking system, or Manual Onboarding — for someone whose prior employment has a scheduled future termination date — a common HR planning practice — the system now correctly classifies this as Rehire with New Employment from the start. Previously, this scenario required extra steps to get the hire type aligned. Now, coordinators reach the right path from the very first click, with no rerouting needed. 

A new setting in Onboarding General Settings — Enable Rehire on New Employment with Future Termination — activates this behavior for your tenant. Once enabled, the routing is permanent and consistent across all future rehires. For employees who have fully completed their prior termination, the profile match screen shows both Rehire with New Employment and Rehire with Old Employment, giving coordinators everything they need in one view to make the right selection. 

Organizations using third-party applicant tracking systems benefit here too: the API now fully supports triggering Rehire with New Employment for candidates with future-dated terminations, removing a prior integration gap. 

One important detail about this setting: it is a one-time activation. In-flight processes continue under their original classification until they complete, so coordinators experience a smooth transition with no disruption to active work. 

WNV: Rehire on New Employment with Future Termination 

Guide: Enabling Rehire on New Employment with Future Termination Date 

Preconfigured Email Templates in Onboarding 

 

 

Full Support for Contractor-to-Employee Transitions 

Features: Rehire with Old Employment for Contingent Worker Conversion  

Organizations with large contingent workforces wanted a seamless path for contractors with a prior full-time employment history to return as permanent employees — and for the system to protect coordinators from accidental selections along the way.  

Rehire with Old Employment for Contingent Worker Conversion 

When a coordinator initiates a rehire for someone who is currently working as a contractor — with a contract end date already set — and that person also has a prior terminated full-time employment record on file, the system now presents Rehire with Old Employment as an option on the profile match screen, pointing directly to the prior full-time record. The contractor's current assignment concludes on its scheduled end date as planned. The prior employment is reactivated. Employment continuity, historical tenure, and record integrity are all preserved. 

The eligibility conditions are clear: the candidate needs an active contingent employment with a scheduled future end date, at least one terminated full-time employment record, and the Rehire with Old Employment feature enabled for the tenant. When all conditions are met, the option appears automatically — no configuration beyond what is already in place. 

Contingent Worker Record Protection 

To give coordinators an even clearer and more reliable profile match screen, all employment records now display a clear role label. Records belonging to contingent workers — contractors, vendors, temporary workers — are visually identified, and the Rehire with Old Employment action for these records is disabled with an explanatory message. This protects coordinators from unintentional selections and keeps the rehire process on the right track. 

WNV: Rehire with Old Employment for Contingent Worker Conversion  

Guide: Converting a Contingent Worker to an Employee 

 

 

Complete Data Merge for Rehire with New Employment 

Feature: Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with New Employment 

Customers running Rehire with New Employment want the data merge to be comprehensive — covering every category of employment data, showing them exactly where each value comes from, and giving them clear guidance when something needs their attention. The merge engine for Rehire with New Employment has been fully rebuilt to deliver exactly that. 

Every data category is now included in the merge. Custom employment fields from the recruiting system transfer correctly to the rehired employment record. Payment information, dependents, emergency contacts, and document attachments are all part of the merge transaction. For attachments, the system automatically updates the Person ID to associate records correctly with the returning employee's new employment. Coordinators see the complete picture — nothing is left behind. 

Field-source transparency is now built in. On the data review screen, each field carries a source indicator showing whether its value originated from the recruiting system, the employee's prior Employee Central record, or the current onboarding process. Coordinators can immediately see where any given value came from and make informed decisions — no cross-referencing required. 

When something needs attention, the system tells you exactly what. If the merge identifies a mandatory field that was not supplied, a data conflict between sources, or a business rule that needs resolving, a dialog presents every affected field by name and category. The coordinator is taken directly to those fields, which are highlighted on the data review screen. The Save button re-enables once the issues are resolved, and the merge retriggers automatically. The result is a focused, actionable correction experience rather than a generic error to investigate. 

For processes that involve a second rehire check, duplicate intermediate records created during that check are cleaned up automatically as part of the merge transaction. Coordinators do not need to take any additional action. 

WNV: Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with New Employment 

Guide: Performing the Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with New Employment 

 

 

Complete Data Merge for Rehire with Old Employment 

Feature: Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with Old Employment 

The same level of data completeness and transparency has been brought to Rehire with Old Employment as well. Customers managing high-volume ROOE processes asked for a merge that covers all employment data, respects locale configurations, and surfaces source information per field. This release delivers all of it. 

Complete data coverage across all entity types. The merge now includes custom employment fields, payment information, dependents, emergency contacts, and attachments — the same full scope available in Rehire with New Employment. Every piece of the employment record transfers correctly into the reactivated employment. 

Locale is respected throughout the entire merge. For employees whose onboarding is configured in a specific language — Dutch, French, German, or any other — the locale, date formats, and name formats are preserved through the full merge process. Coordinators and employees working in non-English environments see their configured language maintained consistently from profile match through to record reactivation. 

Field-source indicators on the Rehire Data Review page. Each field on the review screen shows its origin: recruiting system, the employee's prior EC record, or the current onboarding process. Coordinators reviewing merged data have full context for every value without needing to look elsewhere. 

Clear, structured guidance when correction is needed. As with Rehire with New Employment, when the merge identifies a conflict or missing value, a dialog identifies the specific fields that need attention. The coordinator is taken directly to those fields, corrects them, and the process continues automatically on save. 

WNV: Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with Old Employment 

Guide: Performing the Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with Old Employment 

 

 

Straight to the Next Step When the Merge Is Successful 

Feature: Centralized Service Layer Save for Rehire with Old Employment — Automatic Merge 

With the centralized data merge now handling the full scope of employment data for Rehire with Old Employment, there is a large category of rehires where the Rehire Data Review page does not require any action from the coordinator at all — the system has merged and validated everything correctly, and the record is ready to proceed. 

To reflect this, a new setting — Enable Automatic Rehire Data Merge for Rehire with Old Employment — allows the system to advance past the Rehire Data Review page automatically when the merge completes without any issues. Coordinators move straight to the next step in the onboarding process the moment the profile match is accepted. No additional clicks, no scrolling through data that is already correct. 

The Rehire Data Review page continues to appear exactly when it should: when the merge surfaces a conflict, a missing mandatory value, or a validation issue that genuinely requires a coordinator's decision. In those cases, the coordinator sees the page with only the relevant fields highlighted, resolves them, and the process moves forward. 

This gives the Rehire Data Review page its intended purpose back. It is a place for coordinators to exercise judgment on real data issues — not a step to click through on every clean rehire. 

 

 

The Right Login, Ready on Day One 

Feature: Correct Username Assignment for Rehire with Old Employment 

Customers told us they wanted every returning employee to have a working login from the moment their welcome email arrives — regardless of how many prior employment records exist on file. This is now guaranteed. 

When a coordinator selects a past employment record during Rehire with Old Employment, the system now always sets the returning employee's username to their current personal email address. This update happens simultaneously across the Employee Central user record, the Identity Authentication Service account, and the onboarding record — all before the welcome email is generated. The credentials in the welcome email match the credentials that will grant access, every time. 

For organizations using the Retain Onboarding Username for Rehire with Old Employment setting, that configuration continues to be respected as before. In the default configuration, username alignment is automatic and consistent across all rehires, regardless of how many past employment records a person has in the system. 

Guide: Correct Username Assignment for Rehire on Old Employment | SAP Help Portal 

 

Every Rehire Restart Begins on Clean Ground 

Features: Automatic Anonymization of Intermediate Onboarding Records for Rehires · Prevent Reuse of Cancelled New Hire Records for External Rehires 

Customers asked for a more reliable and predictable experience when restarting onboarding for a candidate whose prior process was cancelled, and for better protection against data from one person's cancelled record affecting another person's onboarding. Both improvements are in place. 

Automatic Anonymization on Cancellation 

When an onboarding process is cancelled, the intermediate record the system created during that process is now automatically anonymized. A new setting — Anonymize Intermediate Onboarding Records on Cancellation — triggers the replacement of identifying personal data (name, national ID, username) with neutral placeholder values the instant a cancellation is processed. The record structure is retained for audit purposes, but the identifying content is gone. Future restarts for the same person, or new processes for different people, proceed cleanly with no interference from the cancelled record. 

Protection Against Cancelled Record Reuse 

The system now ensures that a cancelled external user record is never reactivated when a new onboarding is initiated, regardless of any matching between email addresses. A fresh external user record is always created for every new process. Coordinators and new hires can be confident that each onboarding begins with accurate, current data — always. 

WNV: Automatic Anonymization of Intermediate Onboarding Records for Rehires 

Guide: Performing the Pre-Onboarding Rehire Verification  

 

All Rehire Verification Work, in One Unified View 

Feature: Enhancements to Task Management Page 

Coordinators asked for all their rehire verification work to be accessible from the Task Management page — the central hub where they manage every other onboarding task. All tasks assigned to the Responsible User, including rehire verification tasks, are now available directly from the Task Management page. 

First rehire check tasks have a dedicated home within this experience: the Pre-Onboarding Verification page, which is now accessible directly from the Task Management page. Responsible users with the necessary permissions can navigate to this page to view and act on all first rehire check tasks assigned to them. The page is built for quick identification — it provides search filters for First Name, Last Name, Due Date, and Manager Name so coordinators can locate a specific candidate quickly. Note that the First Name and Last Name fields are standard text fields, not typeahead search fields, so coordinators type the value directly and apply the filter. 

All other rehire-related tasks assigned to the Responsible User are accessible from the main Task Management view alongside the rest of the onboarding pipeline. This gives coordinators a single entry point for their complete task workload — with a clear path to the Pre-Onboarding Verification page when they need to focus on first rehire check activity. 

WNV: Enhancements to Task Management Page 

Guide: Managing Your Onboarding Tasks · Search Filters in Task Management Page 

Search Filters in Pre-Onboarding Rehire Tasks Page

entry.title: Stop MRP requirement transfer when sales order is in approval with supply block
entry.content:
Background

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the flexible approval workflow allows companies to define business rules that route sales orders to approvers before they are confirmed. A common requirement is to hold logistics activities — such as ATP confirmation, Transfer of Requirement (ToR) to MRP, and purchase requisition (PR) creation — while an order is awaiting approval. Starting a procurement run or allocating stock for an order that has not yet been approved by management wastes planning resources and can be difficult to reverse.

In a previous blog, I explained how to stop the Transfer of Requirement to MRP when a sales order enters the approval workflow. That blog covered the configuration approach to prevent MRP requirement transfer for orders pending approval.

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, a new feature called Supply Block extended this capability significantly. Supply Block provides item-level control over all three logistics activities simultaneously — ATP confirmation, ToR to MRP, and PR creation — with a single configuration flag. In this blog, I will explain how to configure Supply Block to work with the approval workflow, and demonstrate the end-to-end behavior with a test scenario.

Business Example

Supply company XYZ uses the flexible approval workflow to manage high-value sales orders. When an order exceeds a certain net value threshold — or when a specific order reason is selected by the sales representative — the order is automatically routed to a sales manager for approval. The sales manager has up to 24 hours to review and either approve or reject the order.

The challenge: between the time the order is saved and the time the manager acts, the system is already running ATP checks, creating MRP requirements, and — for third-party or make-to-order items — generating purchase requisitions. If the manager rejects the order, these logistics activities must be manually reversed. If the manager requests changes, the items may already have been committed to stock or production.

Company XYZ wants all logistics activities to be completely suspended while the approval is pending, and automatically resumed as soon as the order is approved. No manual intervention should be needed to "unblock" logistics after approval. This requirement can be fulfilled through configuration alone — no BAdI implementation is needed.

How Supply Block Integrates with Approval Workflow

Before covering the configuration steps, it is important to understand how Supply Block interacts with the approval workflow.

When a sales order enters the approval workflow, the system evaluates the approval request reason code assigned to the order. Each reason code can be individually configured to trigger Supply Block on all items of the order. When Supply Block is triggered this way, the Supply Block Status field on each item is set to "Blocked". This stops ATP confirmation (confirmed quantity becomes zero), stops Transfer of Requirement to MRP, and prevents PR creation.

Critically, the Supply Block Reason field — the direct, manual supply block field on the item — remains empty. The block comes entirely from the approval workflow configuration. When the approver releases the approval request, the Supply Block Status is cleared automatically across all items, and all three logistics activities resume without any manual intervention.

This is different from a BAdI-driven supply block, where a custom reason code is written to the Supply Block Reason field directly. The distinction matters for troubleshooting: if an order has Supply Block Status = "Blocked" but Supply Block Reason is empty, the block source is either the approval workflow or credit management — not the BAdI.

Step 1: Configure the Approval Request Reasons

The approval workflow in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition uses approval request reason codes to classify why an order requires approval. Reason codes are customer-defined and can be created in the relevant SSCUI.

Go to SSCUI "Define Reasons for Approval Requests" to define a new approval request reason "ZSPB" for supply block. 

Then go to SSCUI "Assign Reasons for Approval Requests" to assign this approval request reason to sales order, and check the indicator of "Supply Block".

Save the configuration and move to BAdI implementation. 

Step 2: Implement Approval BAdI

You can follow SAP help to set up the flexible approval workflow for sales order. Once the flexible approval workflow is configured, you can implement the BAdI SD_APM_SET_APPROVAL_REASON to set the relevant approval request reason based on certain criteria. 

In the BAdI implementation, evaluate the relevant business condition — net value, order reason, profit margin, or any other field available in the sales document context — and assign the appropriate reason code to salesdocapprovalreason.

The following example sets reason code ZSPB  when the order reason is "007" (Fast Delivery). 

* Trigger approval if the order reason is "007"
if salesdocument-sddocumentcategory = 'C' and salesdocument-salesdocumenttype = 'TA' and salesdocument-sddocumentreason = '007'.
  salesdocapprovalreason = 'ZSPB'.
endif.

Save and publish the BAdI implementation. 

Business Process Testing

Create a new standard sales order that meets the approval trigger condition.

Add the item and save the sales order.

Navigate to the Status and Blocks tab. The Overall Supply Block Status shows All Blocked and Approval Status shows In Approval. 

Check the confirmed quantity on the order items. The confirmed quantity is zero — no ATP confirmation has been performed.

Go to app "Manage Material Coverage" and the sales order 11150 is not visible in the requirement list, which means no MRP requirement has been transferred. 

Then approve the sales order. 

After the approval is released, open the sales order 11150 and navigate back to the Status and Blocks tab. The Overall Supply Block Status is now Not Blocked and the Approval Status shows the approval is released.

The confirmed quantity is restored automatically — ATP has re-run.

MRP requirements are transferred, see screenshot below.

Connection to the Previous Blog

The previous blog showed how to stop Transfer of Requirement to MRP when a sales order enters the approval workflow. That approach covered one of the three logistics activities.

With the Supply Block feature in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, the same configuration mechanism now controls all three activities simultaneously:

ActivityPrevious BlogCE2608 with Supply Block

ATP confirmation (confirmed qty)

Stopped via SSCUI 102751 "Set Confirmed Quantities to Zero"

Stopped — same effect, no additional config

Transfer of Requirement to MRP

Workaround only — required "Fixed Date and Qty" flag set manually per item (or via API at creation)

Stopped automatically — no manual steps

Purchase Requisition creation

Not stopped

Stopped

If you implemented the configuration covered in the previous blog, you can extend it by enabling the "Set Supply Block" flag on the same approval request reason codes. The ToR behavior you already have is preserved, and ATP confirmation and PR creation are now also held while approval is pending.

Conclusion

The Supply Block feature in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 provides a straightforward, configuration-only way to hold all logistics activities while a sales order awaits approval. By enabling the Supply Block in sales order approval workflow, companies can ensure that ATP confirmation, Transfer of Requirement to MRP, and purchase requisition creation are all suspended while the order is pending — and automatically resumed upon approval, with no manual intervention needed.

This builds on the standard flexible approval workflow and the previously available ToR-stop capability, filling the remaining gaps in logistics gating. For companies already using the configuration from the previous blog, upgrading to CE2608 and enabling the Supply Block flag on existing reason codes is all that is needed to gain the full three-activity protection.

entry.title: SAP Universal ID Account Linking and Unlinking
entry.content:
What has changed? 

Previously, you could manually link or unlink individual S-user IDs and P-user IDs from your SAP Universal ID via SAP Account Manager. SAP Universal ID no longer serves as the Identity Provider (IdP) for authentication. Users now authenticate through SAP's standard mechanism (e.g. your S-user ID and password through Identity Authentication Service), not through the Universal ID itself. The Universal ID has effectively become an identity "wallet" for managing account associations rather than a login credential. 

This is no longer the case. 

From July 13, 2026, all SAP user accounts that share the same email address are automatically associated with your SAP Universal ID. The option to manually link or unlink accounts has been removed, and the Linked status column has been removed from SAP Account Manager and the Universal ID Console. 

 

What does this mean for you? 

  • If you have multiple IDs registered under the same email address, they will all appear automatically under your SAP Universal ID. 
  • You can no longer unlink a specific S-user or P-user ID from your Universal ID manually. 

 

What if you want an ID removed from your Universal ID? 

There are three options available: 

Option 1 — Update the email address on the ID If you do not want a specific S-user or P-user ID associated with your Universal ID, the email address on that ID can be updated to a different email address. Please contact your Super Admin to arrange this. 

 

Option 2 — Delete the ID If the S-user or P-user ID is no longer required, it can be deleted. 

  • S-user ID deletion can be completed by your Super Admin or by SAP support: How to find your Super administrator   
  • P-user ID deletion is handled by SAP IDS- How to contact IDS: SSO@sap.com  
  • Universal ID deletion is handled by CIC – How to contact CIC: https://support.sap.com/contactus  

 

In both cases, confirmation will be required from the end user before any changes are made. 

Need help? 

If you are unsure which option is right for you, or need assistance, please reach out to your Super Admin in the first instance. 

 For further support, contact SAP through the usual support channels.

entry.title: Re: How do we get SF to mark the SCORM as complete for pa...
entry.content:
@Alanna_OConnell ,  From reading your issue, I understand that you have enabled the Add to History on Failure option for your content, but when users fail the course, the item remains as incomplete on their learning assignments, which causes frustration because the assignment continues to count down to the due date.

The likely cause of the failed item remaining in their assignments would be that the completion status you selected when you checked Add to History on Failure is configured as a Not For Credit completion status. If you go to the item's online content settings, click the gear icon, click the Completion tab, and view the Failure Status listed for the content module that has Add to History Upon Failure, you will see "Not-For-Credit" displaying after the Failure Status ID.  When a completion status is configured as "Not For Credit", the system records a "failure" learning event in the user's learning history, and that completion does not trigger the system to remove the assignment. The system acknowledges the failure in the user's history but requires that they complete the item again until they achieve a passing status. Only a passing status will allow the content to be considered complete, and when all content has been completed, the system will add another learning event to the user's learning history (with a For Credit completion status) and then remove the item from the user's assignments. This is expected system functionality, and it seems that the system is functioning correctly.

But being right does not satisfy the business need you have encountered.  Here are some options, each of which carries their own pros and cons.

1. Tell the users they have to complete the item again and achieve a passing score. Once they achieve a passing score, the item will be removed from their assignments. The failure learning event will remain in their history and can be included in reports, but their history will also show a successful status to confirm they finally did complete the course for credit. In my opinion, this is the BEST OPTION.

2. Create a second item as an alternative option, and set up substitute credit so that if they successfully complete the second item, they get "For Credit" completion for the first item that they failed, which would then satisfy the assignment. This option may not be practicable if you don't have an alternate option already created, and it does require configuring substitute credit, which can be tricky to configure correctly.

3. Manually record learning for the failed item using a For Credit completion status. While this option would remove the item from their assignments, it would also give a false impression that they had successfully completed the item. I DO NOT RECOMMEND this option.

The root of the problem seems to be that users want the system to treat their failure the same way that it treats a successful completion - by giving them credit and removing the assignment. But if a failure status were configured to give credit and allow the assignment to be removed, the user's curriculum containing the failed item would show a false status of Complete and imply that the user was fully qualified in that curriculum, which would not be accurate if one of the required items had been failed.

My recommendation: Get permission from the compliance committee to extend the due dates for this item (at least for those who fail the item), and communicate the expectation that the users who failed the item must complete it again and achieve a passing score - but will be given extra time to do so before going overdue.

Good luck with this situation.  I've been there too.
Mary Katherine
